scope.publicErpSchemas: 1–4 unchanged; no V5 book snapshot exposed to browser or native consumers

invariants.admission: Read-only browser Auth and effective D1 membership/entitlement plus living flags/configuration, then PG grant/opt-in versions; repeated final admission after rendering, hashing and head check. The final rollout read follows the final Auth await. No distributed transaction or arbitrary service-role access guarantee.
invariants.snapshot: Strict selector binds organization, requested financial revision, language, format, invoice or precise report scope. Neutral presentation whitelist omits private book/policy/proofs/credentials/EIN. Actual received/credited/outstanding remain separate exact minor-unit amounts.
invariants.readOnly: The export handler captures read/head ports only; no commit, receipt, tax/provider or Storage operations. Actual PG before/after snapshots verify no financial registry writes across successful exports.
invariants.output: USD/US Letter, bounded rows/text/pages/output, fixed embedded fonts, owned snapshots/fonts/response bytes, exact selector/content SHA256, required Content-Length, safe ASCII attachment filename, no-store and nosniff. A changed head returns409 instead of silently selecting another document.
invariants.browser: Local task feedback preserves invoice/payment draft. A verified download is saved only after bounded transport/header/digest checks; access/context changes discard stale output. Actual browser/download evidence uses a fictitious memory book; PG recipe uses standard Request/Response handlers separately.

limitations: No hosted migration, production/native publication, actual provider call/write or fiscal/accounting certification.
Serialized PGlite and clean NodeFS reopen do not establish real multi-connection contention, crash recovery, load capacity or SLA.
Actual visual/download evidence uses memory V5 and synthetic authority; standard Request/Response PG-handler recipes are separate and use no network socket.
Auth/D1 pre/post fences and transaction-local PG grants/opt-in do not form distributed atomic authority.
Saved metadata and source/test artifacts are evidence, not additional passing tests; the recorder does not rerun checks or inspect screenshots.
Private service credentials remain a trusted-server boundary; this consumer does not restrict arbitrary service-role SELECT access.

rollback.plan: Disable private pilot flags or revoke and advance opt-in/grant versions; retain installed marker, immutable history and existing private book. Never delete the tail or fall back to frozen ERP4.

remaining: Actual hosted/staging authority, multi-connection/race/load/crash validation and provider sandbox/outbox work remain separate approved phases.
Native/public rollout and broader international ERP features remain outside this read-only export extension.
